paper_metadata.title: Characterizing asymmetric and bimodal long-term financial return distributions through quantum walks

summary: The paper studies 31 financial assets and fits their 2-trading-year return distributions with a discrete-time quantum walk using n = 100 steps, or n sampled from N(100, 15^2) over 1000 samples for smoothing. Reported fit quality includes MAE/KS values such as AEP (MAE 0.524, KS 0.456) and PAA (MAE 1.209, KS 1.309), and the authors explicitly state that no asymptotic quantum advantage is claimed.

experiments.description: Discrete-time quantum walk model fitted to empirical long-term logarithmic return distributions of 31 financial assets, including bimodal and asymmetric cases, using a fixed number of steps and a smoothed step-count distribution.

algorithm.variant: discrete-time quantum walk fit for financial return distributions
algorithm.convergence_criteria: optimal parameters identified to precision of 0.0001 radians

hyperparameters.smoothed_time_steps_distribution: N(μ=100, σ²=15²) over 1000 sampled quantum-walk distributions
hyperparameters.histogram_binning: small number of bins; about 20 bins for bimodality assessment
hyperparameters.relative_shift_hyperparameter: used to shift empirical vs quantum-walk distributions
hyperparameters.smoothing_of_quantum_walk_distribution: aggregate each three consecutive non-zero positions into one point

algorithm.parameter_initialization: large set of initial parameter guesses covering parameter space with low resolution

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Quantum walk position probabilities are rescaled and shifted to fit empirical return histograms; no binary-variable encoding used
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize mean absolute error between empirical return histogram Pe(i) and quantum-walk histogram PQW(i): MAE = (1/Nbins) Σ_i |Pe(i) - PQW(i)|

problem_instance.description: Fit long-term logarithmic return distributions of financial assets over ∆t = 2 trading years; focus on bimodal and asymmetric distributions

dataset_specification.date_range: varies by asset; retrieved on 2024-10-14; start dates listed in Table A.2, end dates up to 2024-10-14 or 2024-10-11
dataset_specification.preprocessing: non-trading days excluded; consecutive trading days treated as successive time points; logarithmic returns computed

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Compute logarithmic returns g = log S(t+∆t) - log S(t); use histograms with low resolution to capture global structure; classify distributions as unimodal or bimodal based on local maxima
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Fit all 31 assets; compare quantum-walk fit against Gaussian fit using MAE and KS statistic; selected 12 assets shown in figures; bimodality/asymmetry assessed at ∆t = 504 trading days

noise_model.noise_model: noisy: not applicable; unitary quantum-walk probability distributions computed deterministically

implementation_details.classical_solver: steepest-ascent hill climbing; Gaussian fit used as classical baseline
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: histogram binning; smoothing by aggregating every three consecutive non-zero positions; sampling n from a normal distribution for smoothed fits
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: MAE and KS statistic computed; parameter scatter plots and bimodality/skewness analysis

speedup_claims.caveats: No computational speedup is claimed; the paper is a modeling study and explicitly states that no asymptotic quantum advantage is claimed.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(n^2) for computing the quantum walk probability distribution

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No hardware resources are reported; the work is a noiseless theoretical/simulation study of discrete-time quantum walks with n=100 and a smoothed n ~ N(100, 15^2) fit procedure.
limiting_factors: Classical Gaussian baseline is only a comparison model, not a computational benchmark

notes: No physical quantum hardware is used; the paper presents a theoretical/simulation-based discrete-time quantum-walk model and does not specify a qubit register size, so num_qubits is null/inferred as not reported.
